question: On which river is the Bhakra Nangal Dam constructed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Satluj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhakra Nangal Dam** is constructed on the **Satluj River**, which is one of the major rivers of the Indus river system in India.
 
• The **Bhakra Dam** is located in the state of **Himachal Pradesh**, while the **Nangal Dam** is situated downstream in the state of **Punjab**. Together, they form the Bhakra Nangal Project.
 
• The construction of the dam started in **1948** and was completed in **1963**. This massive project was undertaken to aid in **irrigation**, **power generation**, and **flood control**. Hence, the statement is correct.
 
• The dam is one of the **highest gravity dams** in the world with a height of **226 meters**. It was instrumental in transforming the agriculture of North India, making it self-sufficient in food production.
 
• The water stored in the dam's reservoir, known as the **Gobind Sagar Lake**, is used for multiple purposes such as irrigation, drinking water supply, and hydroelectric power generation.
 
• The project provides water to the states of **Punjab**, **Haryana**, **Rajasthan**, and even parts of **Himachal Pradesh**, contributing significantly to agriculture and industrial activities in these areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Satluj River:**

 
 
• The **Satluj River** originates from the **Raksas Tal** in Tibet, which is located near Lake Mansarovar. It flows through Himachal Pradesh and Punjab before entering Pakistan.
 
• It is the longest of the five rivers of Punjab and is a tributary of the **Indus River**. The river plays a significant role in irrigation and hydropower generation in the northern regions of India.
 
 
 
• **Bhakra Nangal Dam Project:**
 
 
• This project is a symbol of modern India’s engineering and development. It was envisioned to prevent floods in the Satluj-Beas river basin.
 
• The dam generates hydroelectric power with an installed capacity of **1,325 MW**, supplying energy to northern states like Punjab, Haryana, and Delhi.
 
• The **Gobind Sagar Lake**, created by the dam, is one of the largest reservoirs in India, storing up to **9.34 billion cubic meters of water**.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Ravi River:** The Ravi flows through Himachal Pradesh and Punjab but does not host the Bhakra Nangal Dam. It is part of the Indus river system and is used for irrigation purposes.
 
• **Yamuna River:** The Yamuna is a tributary of the Ganga and flows through states like Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, and Delhi. It is not associated with the Bhakra Nangal Dam.
 
• **Ganga River:** The Ganga is the largest river in India, flowing through northern and eastern states, but it does not have any connection with the Bhakra Nangal Dam.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Bhakra Nangal Dam:**

 
 
• The dam is often referred to as the “**Temple of Resurgent India**” by **Jawaharlal Nehru**, as it symbolizes India’s progress and self-reliance after independence.
 
• It has transformed North India into an agricultural powerhouse by providing irrigation water to millions of hectares of farmland.
 
 
 
• **Environmental and Recreational Aspects:**
 
 
• The **Gobind Sagar Lake** is a popular tourist destination, offering boating, fishing, and other recreational activities.
 
• The dam also plays a crucial role in mitigating the risks of floods in the Satluj-Beas river basin, thereby protecting human lives and property.
